findings.title: The kernel carries plan, PR-thread and machine semantics that the domain-free check cannot see
findings.claim: The design calls the kernel domain-free, but several kernel algorithms need to know specific pack kinds, relations and props. The plan fold raises attach.target for 'an accepted next action with no touches'. The reconciler classifies 'unplanned' by an in-progress item's `touches` targets. Projects are fixed to the `plan:<project>` namespace. The `tree` shape returns `Breakdown.threads` (PR addressed/open status), and the `machine`/`checks` shapes read transition props such as event, guard, action, initial and terminal. No mechanism lets the kernel identify these without naming them. Roles (DR-17) bind decision kinds only, not node kinds or relations. The enforcement (`domain_free`: no built-in pack ID followed by '.' in a string literal) catches only literal spellings. So the kernel will either break the literal scan or get these IDs injected ad hoc from `app`, staying domain-coupled in what it does while passing the check.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'A decision kind' roles table: `attach.target` raised by 'the plan fold, for an accepted next action with no `touches`'. 'The reconciler' rule 5: 'not touching an in-progress item's `touches` targets'. 'IDs and aliases': namespace 'plan for plan items'. 'Claims, presence and projects': 'Projects are plans (`plan:<project>`)'. contracts.md PackFile `stages: Vec<StageDecl>, // plan pack only`. contracts.md `Breakdown { ..., threads: Option<ThreadStatus>, touched }` and `MachineView { initial, terminal, variables, ... }`. repo-layout.md `[rust.kernel] domain_free = true # no built-in pack ID followed by "." in a string literal`. DR-17: the kernel 'must name no pack kind (R11, R16)'. DR-15: a new shape 'needs two packs that use it', yet `tree`, `machine`, `checks`, `compare` and `order` each serve one pack. Conflicts with KICKOFF R16 ('The kernel depends on no domain') and R11 ('The core data model is simple, domain-free').
findings.failure_scenario: In M1/M2 an implementer writes `kernel::reconcile` and the attach.target trigger. They need `plan.next_action` and `plan.touches`. Spelled as literals, S15's boundary check (tier A) fails. Built with format!("{}.touches", pack), or passed as constants from `app`, the check passes, but the kernel is still coupled to the plan pack. Replacing or extending the plan pack, or adding a second intent-like domain, then needs kernel edits, contrary to R11. The same applies to PR thread status inside the `tree` shape.
findings.proposed_fix: Pick one option, record it in a DR, and make the check match. (a) Recommended: R14 makes Intent a core idea, so promote the concepts the kernel algorithms need into kernel vocabulary, like `kernel.group` (`kernel.project`, `kernel.item`, `kernel.touches`). The plan pack then supplies only stages, methods, prompts and lint. (b) Alternatively, add declared kind and relation roles in pack data (`[[kinds]] role = "work_item"`, `[[relations]] role = "attach"`), resolved at load like decision roles. Either way, move PR thread status out of the `tree` shape into an artifacts-pack question step. Pass all machine prop names as shape parameters. Extend the domain-free scan to the domain prop names, or replace it with a check that the kernel's public functions take every kind and relation as a parameter.

findings.title: No designed source for a file's or repo's language, so S1's language check and S10's no-'.rb' rule cannot both pass
findings.claim: S1 compares `TRUTH.repos.<repo>.languages`, and platform must report `ruby`. Nothing in the design says where a language is decided. Regex `ExtractorDecl` and `KindDecl` have no language field, the Ruby pack example emits none, and `language` exists only on tree-sitter `Query` extractors for built-in grammars. The natural implementation is an extension table in the universal `files` extractor (crates/extract), which would contain `.rb`. That breaks the S10 rule that no file under crates/ mentions Ruby or .rb. Leaving it out fails S1's language comparison.
findings.evidence: TRUTH.json repos.platform.languages = ['ruby','yaml']. feature_list.json S1 compare: 'TRUTH.repos.<repo>.languages as a minimum'. feature_list.json S10 step: 'a source scan for Ruby, .rb and flags under crates/ outside tests'. architecture.md S10 assertion 5. contracts.md `ExtractorDecl::Regex { id, files, regex, emit }` (no language) and `Query { ..., language: Language, ... }` (closed set of built-in grammars). KICKOFF R1: 'adding a language never touches the core'; S10: 'A new language works through the extractor contract alone.'
findings.failure_scenario: The M1 implementer adds language detection to `extract::files` with a map such as {"rb": "ruby", "go": "go", ...} so S1 passes. In M5, `s10_extensibility.rs::no_engine_source_mentions_the_packs` fails. Removing `.rb` from the map then breaks S1, a tier A scenario.
findings.proposed_fix: Make language identity pack data. Add `[[languages]] id, extensions, line_comment` to `PackFile`, declare the built-in languages (plus yaml and json) in packs/code, and declare `ruby`/`.rb` in examples/packs/ruby. The universal `files` extractor reads the merged table and sets `props.language` on each `code.file`. A repo's languages are the union over its file nodes. Add the field to the contract and the conformance kit.

findings.title: S10's 'no core change' check is mis-specified: it fails on legitimate code and cannot prove what it claims
findings.claim: The S10 CI path asserts that nothing under crates/ outside tests mentions Ruby, .rb or flags, and that `git diff --stat crates/` is empty. By the design's own layout, crates/xtask (`fixture` writes `packs = ["<repo>/examples/packs/ruby"]`) and crates/testkit (the fixture wrapper 'plus the workspace config') must contain the Ruby pack path. 'flags' is an ordinary word in a CLI crate (clap help text, comments about CLI flags, git flags). And `git diff --stat crates/` is empty by construction in any CI checkout, so it proves nothing.
findings.evidence: feature_list.json S10 ci_path last step: 'git diff --stat crates/ (empty) and a source scan for Ruby, .rb and flags under crates/ outside tests'. repo-layout.md: `crates/xtask` and `crates/testkit` live under crates/. 'The one task entry point': `cargo xtask fixture OUT [--no-packs]` writes config 'loading examples/packs/ruby'. Area contracts: testkit owns 'the fixture wrapper (examples/build-fixture plus the workspace config)'. Conventions: 'CLI flags are long-form only'. architecture.md S10 assertion 5. KICKOFF S10 (tier B).
findings.failure_scenario: `no_engine_source_mentions_the_packs` greps crates/ and hits `crates/xtask/src/fixture.rs` ("examples/packs/ruby") and a clap comment about 'global flags'. Either the tier B test fails, or someone narrows it ad hoc mid-milestone, which reads as weakening a scenario without the KICKOFF infeasibility process. Meanwhile the git-diff half passes vacuously, so a real core change made earlier for the toy pack would go unnoticed.
findings.proposed_fix: Restate the check in feature_list.json now, before any code. Scan only the shipped engine crates (contract, kernel, store, extract, models, planroom src and build.rs, plus packs/), excluding xtask and testkit. Match pack identifiers rather than English words (`\bruby\b`, `\.rb\b`, `"flags\.` or a kind-prefix regex), or rename the toy pack to something distinctive (for example `toggles`). Replace the git-diff step with a binary-identity proof: run S10 with the same prebuilt `planroom` binary, by sha256, that ran S1 without the packs, and assert the packs' facts appear only after `PLANROOM_PACKS` is set.

findings.title: Hints carry no ID or provenance, so a linked edge cannot name the pack extractor behind it (an S10 assertion)
findings.claim: S10 asserts that the healthcheck edges' 'provenance is the Ruby pack's extractor through the runtime_wiring linker', and R2 needs 'why do you think A depends on B'. The contract's `Hint` has no `id` and no `provenance`. `Provenance::Linked { linker, hints: Vec<String> }` points at hints by an undefined string. Extractor IDs are also not pack-qualified (`ruby-script`, `ruby-http`), so two packs can declare the same extractor id. A linked edge therefore cannot be traced to the pack and extractor that supplied its input.
findings.evidence: contracts.md `pub struct Hint { kind, scope, key, value, attrs, evidence }` (no id, no provenance), compared with Node and Edge, which both carry `provenance`. `Provenance::Linked { linker: String, hints: Vec<String> }`. `ExtractorDecl::Regex { id: String, ... }` with ids unique only within a pack. architecture.md S10 assertion 4. feature_list.json S10 asserts: 'the healthcheck edges' provenance is the Ruby pack's extractor through the runtime_wiring linker'. KICKOFF R2: 'Every inferred fact shows its evidence and confidence'.
findings.failure_scenario: `healthcheck_edges_through_the_ruby_pack` reads the edge's provenance and finds `Linked { linker: "runtime_wiring", hints: ["platform/tools/healthcheck.rb:orders"] }`, with no way to tell the Ruby pack from any other producer of `code.url` hints. The tier B assertion cannot be checked, and `planroom ask why healthcheck orders` cannot explain which pack inferred the edge. If a second out-of-tree pack also declares an extractor named `ruby-http`, attribution becomes ambiguous.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `id` (a hash of kind, scope, key and evidence) and `provenance: Provenance::Extracted { extractor, tier }` to `Hint`. Make extractor and linker names pack-qualified (`ruby/ruby-http`, `code/runtime_wiring`) and require them to be unique at load. Change `Provenance::Linked.hints` to `Vec<HintRef { id, extractor }>`. Then the S10 assertion and `ask why` can read the chain directly.

findings.title: Declarative emit templates can set only string node props and no edge props, so the toy pack's `enabled` flag can't satisfy its own `when` predicate
findings.claim: A pack declares each kind's props as a JSON Schema fragment, and the fold validates props against it. Decision `when` predicates compare typed values. Yet `EmitTemplate::Node.props` is `BTreeMap<String, String>`, and `EmitTemplate::Edge` has no props at all. The toy pack's `flags.flag` must carry `enabled: false`, a boolean in the truth and in the predicate `{ "props.enabled" = false }`. A declarative extractor can only produce the string "false". That string either fails prop validation (and the fold drops the node) or never equals boolean false, so no `flag_stale` card is raised. Declarative packs also can't attach edge props (versions, `uses`), which the release-style domains need.
findings.evidence: contracts.md `EmitTemplate::Node { ..., props: BTreeMap<String, String>, aliases }` and `EmitTemplate::Edge { edge, from, to, via, confidence }` (no props). `KindDecl { props: Value /* JSON Schema fragment */ }`. architecture.md 'The fold' step 2: 'validate kinds and props against the packs'. 'The decision loop': predicates such as `{ "props.enabled" = false }`. 'The toy domain pack': `flag_stale` on disabled flags. TRUTH scenarios.S10.flags[].enabled is boolean. feature_list S10 assert: 'a flag_stale card exists for gift_wrap'.
findings.failure_scenario: In M5 (2 h budgeted for the toy and Ruby packs), the flags pack's regex captures `enabled: false` as "false". The kind's prop schema says boolean, so validation rejects the node or the `when` predicate never matches. `planroom decide --json` shows no `flag_stale` card and S10 fails. Fixing it needs a change to the contract and the declarative runner in crates/, which is the core change S10 forbids, discovered at the very end of the build.
findings.proposed_fix: Type emit props: allow TOML values or `{ value = "$2", type = "bool|int|number|string" }`, or coerce captures to the type the kind's prop schema declares. Add `props` to `EmitTemplate::Edge` the same way. Add a conformance-kit case in which a declarative pack emits a boolean prop that a `when` predicate selects.

findings.title: Linkers are a closed Rust seam, so pack-declared hint kinds can't be joined without engine changes
findings.claim: Packs can declare `[[hints]]`, but only built-in Rust linkers in crates/extract consume hints, and 'a cross-repo join' must be 'a linker in crates/extract/src/link/'. Two of the six v0.1 domains (observability's `telemetry`, release's `deploys`) already needed bespoke Rust domain logic, not just format parsers. That shows a realistic new domain (k8s selectors, Terraform references, an incident domain) cannot plug in as data. The docs also define 'core' two ways. DR-11 says each new format or join is 'no kernel change', while S10 treats any change under crates/ as a core change. Minor, because the toy pack needs no join and KICKOFF's vocabulary makes the kernel the core.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md 'Where new code goes': 'a cross-repo join → a linker in crates/extract/src/link/'. architecture.md linker table (`runtime_wiring`, `imports`, `deploys`, `telemetry`, each pack-specific Rust). DR-9: 'a pack can't do what the declarative runner and built-ins can't'. DR-11: 'Each is one more built-in or view later, with no kernel change'. feature_list S10: 'git diff --stat crates/ (empty)'. KICKOFF R11: 'New domains plug in as packs without core changes'. Constraints: 'Hand-roll only Planroom's core: the kernel, decision policy, reconciliation and packs.'
findings.failure_scenario: A user writes an out-of-tree `k8s` pack. Regex extractors can emit `k8s.selector` and `k8s.label` hints, but nothing joins them into `deploys` edges until someone adds Rust to crates/extract and ships a new binary. The pack's `[[hints]]` declarations are accepted by the loader yet do nothing, with no warning.
findings.proposed_fix: Add one generic declarative linker, `builtin = "join"` with `options = { left = HINT_KIND, right = HINT_KIND or alias prefix, on = { left_attr = right_key }, emit = EDGE_KIND, via = ATTR }`. It does key equality plus the existing alias resolution, unions evidence, and refuses ambiguous joins as today. Express `deploys`, and the scrape-target half of `telemetry`, with it to prove it. Warn (`unused_hint_kind`) when a pack declares hints no loaded linker consumes. State in one place that 'core' for S10 means the shipped engine crates.

findings.title: The `code` pack is a privileged, unversioned base that out-of-tree packs depend on implicitly
findings.claim: Every pack may require only `[]` or `["code"]`, so the code pack's kinds (`code.file`, `code.tooling`), hint kinds and attrs (`code.url {scheme, host, port, path, method}`), lenses (`runtime`) and linker behaviour are the real extension API. That API has no version range: `requires` is a bare list, and hint attrs are untyped string maps outside the generated schema. It is also exempt from the domain-free rule, and packs can't build on any other domain (an incident pack on `observability.alert`). Calling `code` 'inward' is a choice the docs don't record as one.
findings.evidence: repo-layout.md `[packs] requires = [[], ["code"]]`. contracts.md `PackFile.requires: Vec<String> // [] or ["code"]` and `version: u32`. `Hint.attrs: BTreeMap<String, Value>`. The Ruby pack depends on `code.tooling`, `code.file`, `code.url` attrs and `runtime_wiring` (architecture.md S10 section). KICKOFF R16: 'Packs and adapters depend inward, never sideways'. Constraints release bar: 'versioned public contracts with committed schemas and drift tests'.
findings.failure_scenario: A later code-pack change renames the `code.url` attr `host` to `hostname`, or changes `runtime_wiring`'s join. The Ruby pack still validates (attrs are free strings) and its `doctor --pack` kit passes (it checks only the pack's own emitted facts), but the healthcheck edges silently disappear. An incident-management pack that needs `observability.alert` is refused with `pack_invalid`, so it has to be merged into the core tree.
findings.proposed_fix: Record a DR that `code` is the inward base vocabulary. Give it a version range in `requires` (`requires = { code = "^1" }`), and generate its kinds, hint kinds with typed attrs, lenses and linker names into `docs/reference/packs.md` and the schema, with a drift test. Optionally allow acyclic requires on other packs, checking the pack graph instead of a fixed allow-list.

findings.title: Node ID derivation for pack-emitted nodes is unspecified, and cross-pack collisions merge silently
findings.claim: IDs are `<namespace>:<kind-short>:<key>`, but kind-short is never defined. The examples map `code.service` to `container` and `code.directory` to `dir`, so it isn't simply the kind name. The Ruby pack's `parent = "code.tooling:$stem"` is neither an ID nor an `@alias:` ref, the only two `Ref` forms. Two packs whose kinds map to the same kind-short and key yield the same node ID. The merge rule then unions them and lets the more specific tier win scalar fields, so a pack can overwrite another pack's node unnoticed.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'IDs and aliases' (examples `orders:container:orders`, `storefront:dir:src/cart`). contracts.md `NodeId // "<namespace>:<kind-short>:<key>"`, `pub enum Ref { Id(NodeId), Alias(String) }`. Ruby pack example `parent = "code.tooling:$stem"`. 'Levels and roll-ups': 'When two extractors emit the same node ID, evidence unions and scalar fields take the more specific tier's value'.
findings.failure_scenario: An out-of-tree `terraform` pack declares `terraform.module`. If kind-short is the bare name, `infra:module:vpc` collides with `code.module` nodes of the same key. The pattern-tier pack wins scalar fields, possibly `kind` and `parent`, and the code pack's node is reshaped without a warning. Pack authors also can't predict the IDs their nodes get, so `parent`, `to` and `@alias` templates are guesswork.
findings.proposed_fix: Define ID derivation in the contract: a kind-short declared per `KindDecl` (`id_prefix`), unique across loaded packs and checked at load. Allow `parent`/`to` only as `@id:KIND:KEY` (the engine derives the ID) or `@alias:...`. Make the merge rule refuse, with a warning, to merge nodes whose `kind` differs.

findings.title: Surfaces are outside the domain-free rule, and packs can't say how new kinds and lenses look
findings.claim: The palette keys block colors to code-pack container kinds (service, library, store, infra), and the canvas lens switcher gives each lens a yarn color. But `KindDecl` has only `icon` and `LensDecl` has no color or style, so the surfaces must hard-code pack kind and lens IDs to render them. The domain-literal rule covers only crates/kernel, not `@planroom/ui`, canvas or mod. The Artifact `Snapshot` has fixed `plans` and `machines` fields, and holds maps only 'for the default lenses'. `/room` typeahead comes from the build-time catalogue, so pack questions and lenses never appear in it.
findings.evidence: design-language.md palette `--block-service`, `--block-library`, `--block-store`, `--block-infra`, and Lenses: 'Edge color and style per lens'. contracts.md `KindDecl { ..., icon, empty_text, empty_action }`, `LensDecl { id, label, relations, flow, level, default, ... }`, `Snapshot { maps (default lenses), plans, machines, ... }`. repo-layout.md `[ts.packages]` has no literal scan. KICKOFF S10: a toy pack 'adds kinds, a lens ... with no core change'; R13: three surfaces share one model.
findings.failure_scenario: The toy pack loads, `planroom map --lens flags` works in the CLI, but the canvas shows `flags.flag` blocks in a fallback color, and the yarn switcher shows `flags` with no color or not at all because `@planroom/ui` maps known lens IDs to tokens. The Artifact never includes the flags lens, and `/room ask` typeahead doesn't offer it. Fixing any of this means editing TypeScript in packages/, a surface change for a new domain.
findings.proposed_fix: Add `style` (one of a closed set of design-token slots, such as service, library, store, infra or neutral) to `KindDecl`, and `color` (a token slot) to `LensDecl`/`RelationDecl`. Have surfaces read them from the view model. Extend the domain-literal scan to packages/ui, canvas and mod. Have the snapshot include every loaded lens's top level. Have `/room` typeahead read `planroom ask kinds`/`schema --commands` at session start.

findings.title: Regex extractors can't meet the extractor contract's 'code, not prose' rule, which a new language relies on
findings.claim: The extractor contract requires that code facts come from syntax nodes, never comments or docstrings, and `extract/tests/contract.rs` runs every extractor over a fuzz corpus. A language without a built-in grammar (Ruby, per S10) has only `regex` extractors, which have no notion of comments. So 'a new language through the extractor contract alone' produces facts the contract forbids whenever a URL or require appears in a comment.
findings.evidence: architecture.md 'The extractor contract': 'Code, not prose. Code extractors take string literals and calls from syntax nodes, never from comments or docstrings' and 'Every rule below is checked by extract/tests/contract.rs, which runs every extractor over the fixture and over a fuzz corpus'. contracts.md `ExtractorDecl::Regex { id, files, regex, emit }`. KICKOFF S10: 'A new language works through the extractor contract alone.'
findings.failure_scenario: A Ruby file with `# old endpoint: 'http://orders:8080/v0'` in a comment yields a `code.url` hint and an `http` edge whose evidence is a comment line. The contract test either fails on the Ruby pack's corpus, or exempts regex packs and leaves the rule unenforced for exactly the out-of-tree languages S10 is about.
findings.proposed_fix: Give language declarations (see extensibility-2) `line_comment` and `block_comment` markers, and have the declarative runner blank out comment spans before matching regexes, keeping line numbers. Add a conformance-kit case in which a commented URL must not emit a hint.

findings.title: Boundary rules have two overlapping mechanisms
findings.claim: 'What may depend on what' is expressed twice. Pack `[[rules]]` with `type = forbid_edge` are listed for 'boundary checks', and intended-layer `edit put` edges carry `props.rule = forbid | allow-only`, which the reconciler and the diff engine use. The docs never say which one drift, reconciliation and lint read, or how they interact. That is a duplicated concept with no requirement behind the second form.
findings.evidence: architecture.md pack table: '[[rules]] | ... forbid_edge, covers ... | structural lint, missing artifact parts, boundary checks'. 'Intended architecture and boundary rules': 'Boundary rules for the user's repos ("what may depend on what") are the same forbid and allow-only edits.' KICKOFF R7: 'intended vs actual, including declared boundary rules'. Constraint: 'no speculative abstractions'.
findings.failure_scenario: A pack author writes a `forbid_edge` rule, and a person adds a `forbid` intended edit for the same pair. The rule shows up as a lint finding while the edit shows up as an IntendedVsActual mismatch with a reconcile class. The same violation is then reported twice, in two places with two vocabularies, or a pack-level rule never reaches reconciliation.
findings.proposed_fix: Keep one mechanism. Boundary rules are intended-layer edits, which are authored, versioned, undoable and reconciled. Restrict pack `[[rules]]` to structural lint of authored items (requires_prop, requires_edge, min_children, covers) and drop `forbid_edge`, or define it as sugar that seeds intended `forbid` edits, with one report path.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Kernel algorithms depend on plan-pack vocabulary, and nothing in the design lets the kernel find those kinds and relations without naming them. Roles (DR-17) cover only decision kinds. The enforcement is a literal-string scan, which a kernel that names `touches` without spelling the literal (format!() or constants from `app`) would still pass. In substance this contradicts KICKOFF R16 ('The kernel depends on no domain') and R11. I found no section that passes relation or kind IDs to `kernel::reconcile` or the plan fold as parameters.
verdicts.evidence: architecture.md 'The reconciler (R7)': '`kernel::reconcile(model, plans, history)` ... 5. Unplanned. A change unit ... not touching an in-progress item's `touches` targets'. Roles table: '`attach.target` | the plan fold, for an accepted next action with no `touches`'. DR-17 Context: 'must name no pack kind (R11, R16)', but its Decision binds only decision kinds ('A pack's decision kind binds one with role = ...'). DR-36: 'a scan that no built-in pack kind ID appears as a string literal in crates/kernel/src'. repo-layout.md:127 `domain_free = true # no built-in pack ID followed by "." in a string literal`. contracts.md:453 `Breakdown { ..., threads: Option<ThreadStatus>, ... }` (PR-thread semantics in a kernel shape's view). architecture.md:299: the `plan` namespace is fixed in the ID scheme. KICKOFF.md:117: 'The kernel depends on no domain.'

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. S1 compares repo languages, and the truth requires `ruby` for platform. No document says where a file's or repo's language comes from. The Ruby pack example emits no language prop, and only tree-sitter `Query` extractors carry a `language` field, from a closed set of built-in grammars. The truth also records `language: ruby` for the S10 file. Pack emit props could carry a language string, but the design never says so, and the obvious implementation (an extension map in `extract::files`) would trip S10's `.rb` scan.
verdicts.evidence: TRUTH.json repos: platform languages ['ruby','yaml']; scenarios.S10.ruby.language = 'ruby'. feature_list.json:33 'TRUTH.repos.<repo>.languages as a minimum'. contracts.md:492-493 `Regex { id, files, regex, emit }` (no language), `Query { ..., language: Language, ... }`. architecture.md:577-601: the Ruby pack's emit templates set no language. architecture.md:567: the universal tier emits only file, directory and repo nodes; no language detection is described. A grep for 'languages' across architecture.md, contracts.md and repo-layout.md finds only 'languages/*.toml ... one file per language'.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. As written, the scan covers everything under crates/ outside tests. By the design's own layout, crates/xtask (not a test) must contain the Ruby pack path. 'flags' is an ordinary word that will appear in a CLI crate. A tier B check that fails on legitimate code, or gets narrowed ad hoc, is material. The `git diff --stat crates/` step compares nothing to nothing in a CI checkout, so it proves nothing.
verdicts.evidence: feature_list.json S10 ci_path: 'git diff --stat crates/ (empty) and a source scan for Ruby, .rb and flags under crates/ outside tests'. architecture.md:616: 'No file under crates/ mentions Ruby, .rb or flags outside tests'. repo-layout.md:46 `crates/xtask/ xtask the one task entry point`. repo-layout.md:203: '`cargo xtask fixture OUT [--no-packs]` | ... OUT/.planroom/config.toml loading examples/packs/ruby'. repo-layout.md:98: testkit owns 'the fixture wrapper (examples/build-fixture plus the workspace config)'. DR-13: xtask writes `packs = ["<repo>/examples/packs/ruby"]`.

verdicts.reason: The gap is real: `Hint` has no id or provenance, `Linked.hints` is an undefined `Vec<String>`, and extractor IDs are not pack-qualified. But it does not force S10 to fail. The facts table keys every fact by (snapshot, id), so M1 must define a hint ID anyway. At link time each hint's `FactBatch.extractor` is known, and the opaque `hints: Vec<String>` can carry an extractor-qualified reference without changing the contract's shape. That makes this an under-specified contract detail, not a design that makes the tier B assertion unsatisfiable. Cross-pack extractor-name collisions are a minor robustness issue.
verdicts.evidence: contracts.md:326-333 `pub struct Hint { kind, scope, key, value, attrs, evidence }`. contracts.md:341 `Linked { linker: String, hints: Vec<String> }`. contracts.md FactBatch `pub extractor: String`. architecture.md:442-444 `CREATE TABLE facts (snapshot ..., id TEXT NOT NULL, shape TEXT NOT NULL, ... PRIMARY KEY (snapshot, id))`: hints are facts and need an id that the contract never defines. feature_list S10 asserts: 'the healthcheck edges' provenance is the Ruby pack's extractor through the runtime_wiring linker'.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed. Declarative emit props are string-only, and edge templates have no props. The toy pack's source has `enabled: false` on its own YAML line, so a regex capture yields the string "false". The truth's `enabled` is boolean and the documented predicate form compares with boolean `false`. The design specifies no coercion against the kind's prop schema. So either prop validation rejects the node, or the predicate and the truth comparison don't match, and a fix needs a change to the contract and declarative runner in crates/. That is the core change S10 forbids.
verdicts.evidence: contracts.md:495-499 `Node { ..., props: BTreeMap<String, String>, aliases }` and `Edge { edge, from, to, via, confidence }` (no props). contracts.md:486-487 `KindDecl { ..., props: Value /* JSON Schema fragment */ }`. contracts.md:293 `props: BTreeMap<String, Value>, // validated against the kind's prop schema`. architecture.md:731: predicates such as `{ "props.enabled" = false }`. examples/fixture/repos/storefront/07-feature-flags/tree/flags.yaml:3-4 `gift_wrap:` / `enabled: false`.
